bull.b: Sustained, large free cash flow across the trailing period supports reinvestment, capacity spending, and shareholder returns. High FCF margin increases strategic optionality to fund R&D, secure supply, and execute buybacks without relying on external financing.

A debt-free stance and meaningful cash provide financial flexibility through cycles, lowering insolvency risk and enabling orderly capex, JV investments, or returns. This reduces refinancing risk and supports long-term capacity and supply commitments.

Large multiyear NBMs create durable revenue visibility and higher-margin, predictable streams versus spot NAND sales. Contracted minimums and guarantees underpin planning, support capacity investment decisions, and de-risk revenue volatility over multiple years.

bear.b: Recent rebound follows periods of operating losses and negative cash flow, indicating earnings are cyclical. Persistent negative ROE signals capital has not consistently delivered returns, implying the current strength may be partly cyclical and not yet fully durable.

Variable pricing in long-term contracts reduces guaranteed margin on future volumes; it exposes contracted revenue to market swings and customer renegotiation. This limits predictability of long-term margins and could compress unit economics if spot prices weaken.

Sustaining targeted bit growth necessitates significant dollar capex and cleanroom investment, pressuring free cash flow in expansion phases. Heavy capital intensity raises execution risk and can delay margin improvement if demand or node transitions don't materialize as planned.
